s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: tender lesions on the neck and trunk
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

raw.rationale: The patient has a 10-day history of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and elevated C-reactive protein, which are indicative of an infectious process. The recent chemotherapy and low white blood cell count also increase the risk of infection.

rejected.label: multiple myeloma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of multiple myeloma, the current symptoms and laboratory findings are more suggestive of an infectious process rather than a direct manifestation of the myeloma.
